summary: Sarah McVie's Instagram record on infrastructure centres on chronic flooding and sewage backups in York South–Weston, which she describes as a decades-old problem with one neighbour reporting issues since 1984 (DKxwwGbyDji). She frames the situation as one of floods, property damage, and unmet commitments from elected officials, and generalizes the diagnosis to insufficient, flawed infrastructure planning tied to irresponsible development elsewhere in the city (DZXc9u9xRn6). Alongside these positions, she documents concrete organizing: co-founding the Black Creek Flood Coalition beginning with neighbour meetings in January 2025, and delivering 200+ petition signatures to City Hall in June 2025, including an envelope addressed to the Mayor after the local councillor did not appear (DKxwwGbyDji). The stance across records is consistent in identifying local infrastructure as neglected and demanding municipal accountability.

key_positions.stance: Characterizes flooding and sewage backups in York South–Weston as long-standing infrastructure failures, citing a neighbour who has reported issues since 1984.
Describes residents as having endured floods, property damage, and unmet commitments from elected officials.
Frames the broader problem as insufficient and flawed infrastructure planning, linked to irresponsible development patterns in other neighbourhoods.

key_actions.action: Co-founded the Black Creek Flood Coalition in January 2025, beginning with neighbour meetings in York South–Weston to organize around chronic flooding.
Delivered 200+ petition signatures to City Hall in June 2025, handing one envelope to a councillor's staffer and leaving a second envelope addressed to the Mayor.
